items.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources. With RAG, LLMs first refer to a specified set of documents, then respond to user queries. These documents supplement information from the LLM's pre-existing training data. This allows LLMs to use domain-specific and/or updated information that is not available in the training data. For example, this enables LLM-based chatbots to access internal company data or generate responses based on authoritative sources. The technique was first proposed in 2020 and has since become a widely adopted approach in modern AI systems.

items.title: it’s f*cking insane
items.summary:
it’s f*cking insane
the scariest thing i found with claude in 2026 was inside my AirPods Max

i bought them second-hand. looked perfect. sounded perfect. connected to my laptop like any other pair

after writing my article about bugs and hidden cameras, i asked Claude to check every Bluetooth device on my laptop too

6 devices. 5 clean. and then this ↓

"AirPods Max":
→ firmware version that doesn't exist in Apple's release list
→ secretly registered as a KEYBOARD too, hidden from the menu
→ microphone open 14 hours a day. no call. no app using it

and 2 days after i first paired them, an app called "BTAudioSync" appeared on my laptop. i never installed it

it recorded everything through the headphone mic and uploaded it every night at 3am

5 weeks of my life:
→ 1,284 audio clips
→ 63 hours of audio
→ 41 uploads to a server i'd never heard of

meetings. calls. me alone in my room

to be clear: this isn't Apple spying on anyone. this pair was tampered with before it ever reached me. a second-hand device can be anything inside

what Claude helped me do in one evening:
→ disconnected and forgot the headphones
→ removed the app and everything that launched it
→ blocked the upload server and deleted the clips
→ set mic access to apps i approve only
→ reset Bluetooth and re-paired only devices i trust
→ saved everything as evidence

if you bought headphones, a keyboard or a mouse second-hand, check what it really is before you trust it

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”
